title: Microsoft Purview DLP: test files against all classifiers (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, existing test controls and role-group instructions are supported. It distinguishes the new government-cloud file test from documented per-type testing and keeps the new test's licensing, default and permissions explicitly unresolved.

claims.claim: This is a Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention file-testing feature.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention - File Testing Against Sensitive Information Classifiers

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a new test function on the main Classification page.
claims.quote: A new feature will be introduced on the main Classification page

claims.claim: The planned function tests files against all available classifiers to identify sensitive information.
claims.quote: allowing users to test files against all available classifiers to identify the presence of sensitive information.

claims.claim: Users can select a single classifier instead of testing across all classifiers.
claims.quote: Users will have the option to select a single classifier or run tests across all classifiers.

claims.claim: The stated purpose is finding sensitive content and troubleshooting classification issues more efficiently.
claims.quote: This capability is designed to help users identify sensitive content within files and troubleshoot classification issues more efficiently.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the new all-classifier file test in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "all classifiers" "test"; opened data-classification-overview, sit-test-a-sit and sit-sensitive-information-type-learn-about. Results describe the overview, per-type testing and unrelated classification capabilities, not this new test.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The Purview portal's Classifiers page is accessible under Information Protection, Data Loss Prevention or DSPM.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, you can access Classifiers under Information Protection, Data Loss Prevention, or DSPM (Data Security Posture Management).

claims.claim: The roadmap does not identify Learn's Classifiers page as its main Classification page.
claims.quote: A new feature will be introduced on the main Classification page, allowing users to test files against all available classifiers

claims.claim: Learn marks the new Classifiers experience as preview, distinct from this roadmap item's General Availability phase.
claims.quote: The new Classifiers experience in Microsoft Purview is in preview and is available alongside the existing classification experiences.

claims.claim: The existing per-type test is at Microsoft Purview portal > Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types > sensitive information type > Test.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Information Protection > Classifiers > Sensitive info types and choose the sensitive information type from the list to open the details pane. Choose Test.

claims.claim: The existing per-type portal test accepts an uploaded file.
claims.quote: Upload a file and choose Test.

claims.claim: The existing per-type portal procedure supports only unencrypted files.
claims.quote: This procedure is only supported for unencrypted files.

claims.claim: The existing per-type portal test uploads and tests one file at a time.
claims.quote: You can only upload and test one file at a time.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated that the new all-classifier test inherits the per-type test's file-count or encryption limits.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview test files all classifiers limits file types encrypted size GCC GCC High DoD. Opened data-classification-overview and sit-test-a-sit; the latter documents per-type limits, not their applicability to the new test.

claims.claim: The existing uploaded-file test displays match results for the uploaded file.
claims.quote: It tests the SIT against the file you upload; On the Match results page, review the results and choose Finish.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The existing uploaded-file test does not refresh classification for existing SharePoint or OneDrive files.
claims.quote: It tests the SIT against the file you upload; it doesn't refresh classification for existing SharePoint or OneDrive files.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The same SIT can return different results for email in transit, files at rest and files on managed devices.
claims.quote: The same sensitive information type can produce different results depending on where content is evaluated—for example, email in transit (Exchange), files at rest (SharePoint and OneDrive), and files on managed devices (Endpoint DLP).

claims.claim: Test-DataClassification -ClassificationNames <names> -TextToClassify <text> is a documented classification test call.
claims.quote: Test-DataClassification [-ClassificationNames <String[]>] ... [-TextToClassify <String>]; ClassificationNames ... Valid values are: Name; Id (GUID value). You can specify multiple values separated by commas.

claims.claim: The printed cmdlet call tests a specified text string rather than uploading a file.
claims.quote: Use the Test-DataClassification cmdlet to find the confidence and count of a sensitive information type that's found in a specified text string.

claims.claim: Purview role-group membership is managed through Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. ... select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. ... On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user>" adds a member to a role group and grants its roles' permissions.
claims.quote: Add-RoleGroupMember [-Identity] <RoleGroupIdParameter> -Member <SecurityPrincipalIdParameter>; When you add a member to a role group, the member is given the effective permissions provided by the management roles assigned to the role group.
